summary: Obfuscated agent daemon executes remote commands from a WebSocket gateway
details: @whalent/agent ships a daemon (`whalent`) that connects to a WebSocket gateway (default first-party at Whalent Memory, overridable via `--gateway`) and, per the package's own README, accepts remote commands (including `upgrade`, `restart`) driven by the gateway. The shipped bundle depends on `node-pty`, `@xterm/headless`, `ssh2`, and `ws`, and contains many `terminal` / `shell` / `command` / `remote` string references consistent with a remote party driving a local PTY/shell on the installer's host. Both `dist/index.cjs` and the ~13 MB `dist/core.cjs` are heavily obfuscated using javascript-obfuscator (rotated string array + wrapper decoders, `_0x`-hex identifiers, control-flow flattening); `javascript-obfuscator` is listed in the package's own devDependencies. The obfuscation makes the gateway-to-shell dataflow inside the daemon opaque to review. Installing and running the daemon exposes the host to full-host command execution driven by whoever controls the connected gateway.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
